html:
The Ñancahuazú Guerrilla was a small rebel band led by Che Guevara in southeastern Bolivia from late 1966 to October 1967. It ended with Guevara's capture and execution.

Guevara, hero of the Cuban Revolution, hoped to start a revolution that would spread across South America. He chose a remote area near the Ñancahuazú River. But the local peasants, many of whom had received land in the revolution of 1952, did not join, and the Bolivian Communist Party gave little help.

The Bolivian army, trained and advised by the United States, hunted the band down. Guevara was captured on 8 October 1967 and shot the next day in the village schoolhouse of La Higuera. Photographs of his body made him an icon, and his bones were found and returned to Cuba in 1997. The failure in Bolivia marked the limits of exported revolution.
sum: The Ñancahuazú Guerrilla was a small rebel band led by Che Guevara in southeastern Bolivia from late 1966 to October 1967. It ended with Guevara's capture and execution.
